extracted.intended_audience: travellers and art-lovers visiting Venice; readers learning how to look at and judge paintings, sculpture, and architecture on-site
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for observing and judging works of painting, sculpture, and architecture in Venice — what to notice (composition, color, finish, symbolism, viewing distance, preservation) and how technical/contractual/contextual factors affect aesthetic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition in concentric zones with central focal figures
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole composition is divided into concentric zones, represented one above another, like the stories of a cupola, round the figures of Christ and the Madonna at the central and highest point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note how the painter arranges bands/zones of figures toward a central focal point; examine dignity and beauty of the central figures and the way surrounding zones direct attention toward them. Look for supporting elements (e.g., white distances filled with floating spirits) that reinforce the concentric plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmony (classical academic expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Venetian academicians declare [some works] to want harmony — implying harmony is an expected quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that academic 'harmony' may be a conventional standard; divergence from academic harmony is not necessarily a defect (author defends works that lack 'harmony' as possessing other virtues). Weigh harmony against other qualities like daring conception or dignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overpopulating narrative scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: In battle pieces the figures, like the arrows, are put in by the score; the painter seems ordered to represent all events of the battle at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware of works that try to depict every event simultaneously — quantity of figures can satisfy patrons but reduce artistic coherence. Prefer compositions that prioritize clarity of narrative or a unified impression over exhaustive illustration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical interest versus artistic merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Various pictures are only historically, not artistically, interesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish whether a work's value is documentary/historical or whether it has intrinsic artistic qualities; both kinds of interest exist, but they are different criteria for appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity and correct attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The traveller must be warned against mistaking the works of Domenico Robusti (Domenico Tintoretto) for those of his illustrious father, Jacopo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check attribution and provenance; unsigned or repainted works may mislead. Correct attribution affects how one judges quality and importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feeling and subtlety of conception
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of Titian's want of feeling and coarseness of conception are striking even when a work is of great value as art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge not only technical execution but the artist's emotional subtlety and depth of conception — a work can be technically fine yet coarse or lacking feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of distance and indistinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine carefully the mode of painting the Venice in the distance — Turner's indistinctness of touch is mentioned for comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe how distant elements are rendered (distinct vs indistinct) and how that treatment contributes to atmosphere and depth; indistinctness can be a deliberate, skilled device, not a fault.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of studying even damaged works
rubrics_metrics.description: Frescoes once magnificent, now mere wrecks (plaster crumbling), yet deserving of the most earnest study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Damage or decay does not remove the pedagogic or aesthetic value of a work; study technique, composition, and conception even in ruined pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended viewing distance and vantage
rubrics_metrics.description: Some works (e.g., 'Christ taken down from the Cross') are executed for distant effect and are seen best from the end of the room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess where the painter intended the work to be viewed from; approach paintings from the proper vantage to judge color, scale, and effect as intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daring conception versus carelessness
rubrics_metrics.description: Works notable for the sweep of vast green surges and daring conception may be wild and careless and in many respects unworthy of the master.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appreciate bold imaginative qualities, but also critique carelessness of execution; a daring idea needs adequate control and finish to be fully successful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioned work vs. inspired work
rubrics_metrics.description: Study what a great man does 'to order' when wearied of what is required from him — commissioned pieces can show weariness and formulaic responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether a work was produced to commission under constraints; evaluate how the artist responds to commissions (does he seem to have given his best or to have complied mechanically?).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finish, tone, and sober tints
rubrics_metrics.description: Pictures with excessively little color, prevalent greyish-brown tones, thinly painted, perfect in tone, and quite untouched — approaching grisaille yet delicious pieces of color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value restraint in palette, mastery of tone, and subtlety of limited coloration; sober tints and thin handling can achieve refinement superior to bright, ornate coloring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of exquisite care and freedom of execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Every line of leaves and olive branches studied with the most exquisite care, and yet cast with perfect freedom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for a balance where fine study and detailed observation coexist with a free, expressive hand; both are virtues when combined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation, light exposure, and repainting risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Once noble works now miserably faded because the sun was allowed to fall on them all day long; repainted works risk losing original interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how preservation conditions (light, exposure) and interventions (overpainting/retouching) have altered a work; prefer original, well-preserved surfaces when possible and be cautious about repaints that alter the artist's intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality vs. reliance on common models
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Vulcan and the Cyclops' is a singularly meagre and vulgar study of common models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique works that rely on rote models or stock types rather than original invention; originality matters in evaluating artistic worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of frank (bold) color
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the grandest pieces of frank color in the Ducal Palace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge how boldly and honestly color is used — 'frank' color can be a virtue when it is purposeful and integrated into composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalistic treatment of delicate effects (e.g., veils)
rubrics_metrics.description: Note how a veil falls showing the sky through it, like an alpine cascade falling over a marble rock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe and praise the painter's skill in rendering transparent fabrics and other subtle visual effects that integrate figure and environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to minor details (wings, carpets, accessories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Note especially the painting of the lion's wings, and of the colored carpet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor elements can reveal an artist's meticulousness and character; examine accessories and small features as evidence of craft and taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of architectural devices: light, shadow, and cavity
rubrics_metrics.description: A dark penetration (cavity) is often a most precious assistance to a building dependent upon color for its effect; a circular penetration surrounded by deep russet marble moulding is beautifully used in St. Mark's.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging architecture, note how the architect uses shadow and structural cavities to enhance color and sculptural effect; critique purely formal solutions that ignore such considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation choices to convey temporal continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: Tintoret indicates the continuity of the supply of heavenly food in 'Gathering the Manna' by showing varied everyday activities rather than a hurried crowd gathering manna.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether compositional choices (showing ongoing activity vs a single moment) effectively convey time and narrative intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of light to signify sacredness and imaginative transformation
rubrics_metrics.description: In 'The Last Supper' the strong light shining from the head of Christ and the smoke of the lamp turning into a multitude of angels mark the subject as sacred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how lighting and poetic devices (e.g., smoke forming angels) are used to convey spiritual or symbolic meaning; technical mastery of candlelight and mixed light sources is a key evaluative point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carefulness versus haste and the effects of damage
rubrics_metrics.description: Some pictures appear hastily painted and are disagreeable owing to violent color changes; haste shows in less finished passages and damages alter original effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between deliberate loose handling and slovenly haste; consider whether visible signs are artist's method or later degradation; color shifts (e.g., red turned violent) often indicate damage or poor restoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portraiture within religious composition — compositional tradeoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Some works are painted more for the sake of the included portraits (chamberlains) than for the religious subject; as an 'Adoration' the scene may be absurd but as portraiture and composition it can be perfect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When portraits are included in religious scenes, judge both the success as devotional imagery and as portrait/compositional achievement; anachronism or idealization may be acceptable if the work clearly signals its imaginative intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolic detail and subtle narrative devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Small details (a leaf crumpled, a book crushed) carry symbolic meaning — e.g., the crushed book indicates the Mosaic history violated by Stephen's murderers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for symbolic uses of seemingly minor elements and how they reinforce narrative or theological points; these devices often show the painter's intelligence and depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restraint in depiction of violence
rubrics_metrics.description: Covering the ground with piles of stones yet leaving the martyr apparently unwounded — the painter chooses not to make his picture disgusting or painful; the martyr's face is serene and exulting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate decisions to withhold graphic horror in favor of dignity and spiritual meaning; restraint can be morally and artistically powerful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery of large-scale multi-figure composition
rubrics_metrics.description: A large crucifixion contains fifty figures with none contending with another; decision in arrangement of masses of light, infinite half tones and modulations, magnificence of handling; little conceded to haste or accident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise works that achieve unity and clarity across many figures through controlled handling of light, color, and mass; note absence of hurried execution and evidence of careful planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of small compositional devices to prevent heaviness
rubrics_metrics.description: Accumulated forms of human body are prevented from being felt heavy by the grace and elasticity of two or three sprays of leafage which spring from a broken (cut) root.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how small elements (foliage, light spots) are employed to relieve compositional density and add symbolic resonance; appreciate subtle devices that improve overall balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for medium-specific integrity in sculpture
rubrics_metrics.description: The sculpture round the altar is an example of the abuse of the sculptor's art — every accessory labored to turn sculpture into painting, with grass, trees, and landscape realized in alto-relievo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge sculpture by its own medium's strengths; avoid critiquing sculptural reliefs that attempt to imitate painting; recognise when artists overwork accessories to the detriment of medium integrity.
